items.headline: Herzog accepts the results and opens coalition talks
items.summary: Israel's president called the certified count legally binding and began meetings with party leaders, with neither Netanyahu's 53 seats nor Eisenkot's 48 enough to govern.
items.matters: the mandate he hands out in the next few days decides whether Netanyahu stays.
items.body: Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has accepted the certified results of last week’s parliamentary elections and begun consultations with party leaders on whom to task with forming the next government. The moves on Wednesday dealt a blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s efforts to discredit the vote, in which he and his allies lost their majority in the 120-member parliament, while Arab-led parties made historic gains. In the October 27 vote, neither Netanyahu’s coalition nor the bloc of his chief rival, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, secured the 61 seats required to govern. The prime minister’s coalition won 53, while Eisonkot’s got 48. That leaves open the possibility of an alliance between the two men or an alliance between Eisenkot and the Arab-led parties – Ra’am and the Joint List – which had secured a record 19 seats. Herzog concluded the first day of consultations with party leaders on Wednesday night, and said talks would continue on Thursday. On Wednesday, the president said he met with representatives of the Religious Zionism and Zehut, Shas, and Yisrael Beytenu factions. He “received their recommendations regarding the identity of the Knesset member upon whom the task of forming the government should be assigned,” Herzog said on X. Three factions aligned with Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist base recommended that the prime minister be given a chance to form a coalition, while a fourth, led by a former Netanyahu ally turned rival, backed Eisenkot. Eight more parties, including the two Arab-led factions, are scheduled to meet with the president on Thursday, with Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Netanyahu’s Likud going last. Eisenkot’s prospects improved when Ra’am, a major Arab-led party, said it would recommend him. That brought his expected support to 56 lawmakers, according to the Israeli news site Ynet, which is still short of a majority. The other Arab-led party, the Joint List, has not announced its position. Israel’s Channel 12 reported that the party was expected to coordinate with Eisenkot, endorsing him if asked or abstaining if he preferred. Its 11 seats could push him past 61. Degel HaTorah, which holds four of United Torah Judaism’s seven seats, said it would recommend neither candidate. The ultra-Orthodox faction broke with Netanyahu over his coalition’s failure to pass legislation exempting Haredi men from military service, The Times of Israel reported. Once the consultations end, Herzog will choose the candidate he considers best placed to assemble a coalition, almost certainly Netanyahu or Eisenkot. He has several days to…

items.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to ten more years
items.summary: Hong Kong's High Court imposed the term for colluding with foreign forces, ruling the offence grave; he had been due for release in January and now faces late 2036.
items.matters: the sentence shows Beijing will keep its best-known prisoner past the point where release had become thinkable.
items.body: Wong is among hundreds of campaigners and ordinary Hongkongers arrested under the law, which was imposed in 2020 following explosive pro-democracy protests against Beijing's growing control. Critics say the far-reaching law has silenced dissent, but authorities argue that it is needed to maintain stability and deny it has weakened the city's cherished autonomy. Having already spent the last six years in jail, Wong, who was due to be freed in January, will now spend another decade behind bars. Wong, who turned 30 last month, has already been imprisoned multiple times for his activism which started when he was in his early teens. On Thursday, he arrived in court wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt, khaki trousers and black-rimmed glasses. He looked slimmer compared to his previous public appearances. He nodded in greeting towards members of the packed public gallery, and took notes intermittently as the judge read out the reasons for his sentencing. A crowd had gathered outside the court, with dozens of Hongkongers having queued for hours hoping to get a seat in the public gallery. There was also a heavy police presence. Wong is already serving time for subversion and was due to be freed early next year when he was handed the latest charges, to which he pleaded guilty in September. Two months and two days of the 10-year term will be served concurrently with his ongoing sentence, the judge said on Thursday. Prosecutors said Wong had conspired with other campaigners, including self-exiled activist Nathan Law, to lobby for foreign sanctions and blockades against Beijing. On Thursday, Hong Kong's chief executive John Lee said Wong and Law were "among the primary culprits responsible for undermining Hong Kong's prosperity and stability". Their actions "not only severely undermined national sovereignty, security, and development interests, but also directly prejudiced the well-being of the general public and the stability of society," Lee said in a statement issued after the ruling. Beijing's foreign ministry said China "firmly supports [Hong Kong] in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law". It also called on "relevant parties" to "earnestly respect China's sovereignty and Hong Kong's legal system". Wong's friend and fellow activist Frances Hui, now based in the US, said she was "heartbroken" and "outraged" by the verdict. "Today's sentencing is not just about Joshua. It is part of a broader political crackdown that seeks to rewrite a chapter of Hong Kong's history and erase the contributions of an entire generation who believed they could…

items.body: W środę 4 listopada rano funkcjonariusze Centralnego Biura Antykorupcyjnego przeprowadzili akcję dotyczącą nieprawidłowości związanych z elektrownią Ostrołęka. Na polecenie prokuratury zatrzymano 25 osób. Węgiel Błędy w rozliczeniu węglowej Ostrołęki Działania Elektrowni Ostrołęka związane z wycofaniem się z budowy bloku węglowego i z rozliczeniem były nielegalne – ocenia NIK. Jak wynika z wypowiedzi ministra, zatrzymania stanowią początek intensywnych działań mających na celu wyjaśnienie sprawy. – Po bardzo dużej pracy CBA i prokuratury podjęliśmy działania w celu rozliczenia tej sprawy – powiedział polityk na antenie TVN24. Jak zaznaczył, chodzi o „wszystko, co jest wokół elektrowni Ostrołęka”. – Budowę bloków, zmarnowane pieniądze, powiązani samorządowcy, powiązane firmy – podkreślił. Jak wskazał Siemoniak, dziś rano CBA na zlecenie prokuratury zatrzymało 25 osób. – Zabezpiecza w tym momencie różne dokumenty, przeszukuje różne lokale – wskazał, dodając, że „w pierwszym rzucie są to osoby może nie z pierwszych stron gazet”. – Ale pamiętamy powagę tej afery. Pamiętamy miliardy, które poszły i niewątpliwie ta sprawa ma charakter wybitnie rozwojowy – stwierdził. – Zaczynamy tę sprawę bardzo aktywnie wyjaśniać i będzie to ogromne śledztwo. Dzisiaj machina ruszyła – powiedział koordynator służb specjalnych. Jak przekazał we wpisie opublikowanym w serwisie X Siemoniak, śledztwo obejmujące lata 2018-2019 dotyczy działania na szkodę spółek Elektrownia Ostrołęka Sp. z o.o., Enea SA oraz Energa SA poprzez niedopełnienie obowiązków przez członków zarządów i rad nadzorczych. „Oszacowano, że wyrządzona szkoda majątkowa wielkich rozmiarów przekracza 1 mld zł. Czynności z udziałem zatrzymanych – przeszukania i zabezpieczanie materiałów dowodowych – prowadzone są w 30 miejscach na terenie 11 województw” – wskazał. Elektroenergetyka Szef GE Vernova odczarowuje Ostrołękę. „To nie porażka, lecz dobry wybór” Gazowa elektrownia w Ostrołęce powinna być przykładem racjonalnych decyzji w obliczu zmieniającego się otoczenia, a nie klęski. Elektrownia gazowa... Do sprawy odniósł się także podczas briefingu prasowego Jacek Dobrzyński, rzecznik koordynatora do spraw służb specjalnych. – Wszyscy zatrzymani zostaną przewiezieni jeszcze dzisiaj do prokuratury regionalnej w Białymstoku. To ona na podstawie materiałów zgromadzonych przez agentów CBA wszczęła to śledztwo. Podkreślam – jest to poważna szkoda w mieniu. items.body: Asia stocks mixed as chip rout triggers KOSPI trading halt; China outperforms Ayushman Ojha Thu, November 5, 2026 at 5:24 a.m. GMT+1 3 min read 005930.KS ARM QCOM ^IXIC CL=F Investing.com-- Asian stocks were mixed on Thursday, as a sharp selloff in semiconductor shares triggered a trading curb in South Korea, offsetting support from a steep decline in oil prices after Democrats' victories in the U.S. midterm elections. U.S. stock futures were also mixed during Asian hours by 07:18 GMT, with tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Futures leading losses. Wall Street closed higher overnight as investors welcomed the prospect of Democrats gaining control of Congress. South Korea's KOSPI closed 5.3% lower, after triggering a sell-side trading curb earlier in the day, as a sharp selloff in semiconductor stocks intensified. Heavyweight chipmakers Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) and SK Hynix Inc (KS:000660) slumped 7.6% and 9.5%, respectively. The losses came as disappointing earnings from U.S. chip designers Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) and Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) revived concerns over the semiconductor industry's growth outlook. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had dropped 3.1% overnight to a six-month low. Chip equipment makers also came under pressure, reflecting concerns about weaker smartphone demand, rising memory costs and uncertainty over the returns from massive artificial intelligence investments. Japan's chip and artificial intelligence-related shares also extended their losses on Thursday, following a steep selloff in the previous session. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest (TYO:6857) fell 14.7%, while Lasertec (TYO:6920) dropped 14.2% and Kioxia Holdings (TYO:285A) declined more than 13%. Technology investor SoftBank (TYO:9984) slid 7%. Chinese stocks bucked the regional technology selloff, with semiconductor shares advancing as Beijing's fresh support measures boosted investor appetite for domestic chipmakers. The blue-chip Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 index rose 0.3%, while Shanghai Composite edged up 0.1%. Chinese semiconductor shares benefited from the People's Bank of China's decision to cut the interest rate on its relending facility for share buybacks and share purchases by 25 basis points to 1%. Beijing's push to reduce reliance on U.S. semiconductor technology also continues to support domestic chip designers, foundries and equipment manufacturers. Losses across Asia were capped by a more favourable macroeconomic backdrop after oil prices plunged on Wednesday. items.body: The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 3%, or over 1,500 points, marking its best single-day performance since President Trump paused a sweeping tariff rollout in April 2025. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) climbed 1.6%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) traded up by 1.4% amid a post-election relief rally. Markets swiftly repriced a Democratic sweep of the House and Senate — and the potential for ballot measures and newly elected officials to restrict data center construction . Chip stocks, including Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Micron ( MU ), fell. Meanwhile, other parts of the tech sector offset some of those losses, with Apple ( AAPL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) each hitting all-time highs. Oil prices plunged as the midterm election outcome also raised hopes for an end to the war in the Middle East. Brent crude oil futures ( BZ=F ) dropped 8% to around $95 per barrel. Investors will also be watching in the coming weeks for policy actions on housing and pharmaceuticals in the aftermath of the election. As Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre pointed out on Tuesday , midterm elections have a history of shaping stock performance in the near term but don't tend to move markets much over the long term. On the economic front, ISM and S&P data showed that US services activity expanded at a slower pace in October as businesses continued to grapple with elevated costs. Private-sector hiring , meanwhile, continued to show strength in October as an ADP report indicated "pretty solid job growth." Earnings continue to roll in. AMD ( AMD ) posted a Q3 earnings beat , while McDonald's ( MCD ) grappled with slowing same-store sales growth . Duolingo ( DUOL ) stock soared over 30% on strong user growth. US stocks rallied Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, as investors embraced the prospect of divided government and rotated into several of the market's biggest technology names. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) rose 3%, marking its best single-day performance since President Trump paused a sweeping tariff rollout in April 2025. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained 1.5%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed 1.4%. Oil prices plunged amid the rally in stocks, with West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) falling more than 7.7% below $90 a barrel. items.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: the company says it leads on agentic coding and knowledge work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.
items.matters: a cheaper frontier model resets the price of every coding agent built on top of it.
items.body: We’re introducing Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in our new Claude 5.5 family. It performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5. Claude Opus 5.5 is our first release since we called for pacing the frontier . It was tested before release by external evaluators, including Frontier Design and METR . On our automated behavioral audit, the most comprehensive alignment test we run, Opus 5.5 is the strongest-performing model we’ve tested to date. It also comes with the safeguards we’ve developed for our most capable models. Performance. Opus 5.5 is a major step up from Opus 5. It’s the new leading model, and early testers saw large jumps in performance on their most complex work. One tester completed a 680,000-line code migration in less than a day—work that would have taken an engineering team weeks. It’s good at finding and fixing inefficiencies in software: when we asked it to cut load times across every page of a web app, Opus 5.5 succeeded 39 of 40 times, while Opus 5 made smaller improvements that also altered the app’s behavior. A different tester had several Claude models build a game from a single prompt; Opus 5.5 scored higher than any other model on the strength of its graphics and polish. Safety. Opus 5.5 achieves the best scores of any model to date on our automated behavioral audit, our alignment suite that tests Claude across thousands of simulated scenarios. It is much less likely than recent models to take hard-to-reverse actions or act outside the boundaries it’s been given, and it’s more resistant than Opus 5 to prompt injection. We’ve also broadened our alignment testing to cover longer tasks, impossible tasks, and scenarios modeled on real incidents, though it still has limits. Full details of our evaluation are available in the Opus 5.5 System Card . Because Opus 5.5 is comparable to Claude Mythos 5.1 in biology and cybersecurity, we’re deploying it with safeguards similar to those on Claude Fable 5.1. Vetted organizations can apply today to our Life Sciences Verification Program to use Opus 5.5 for biology research. In the coming weeks we will also be expanding access to our Cyber Verification Program , and verified cybersecurity practitioners will be able to use Opus 5.5 for their work. Cost and speed. Opus 5.5 requires less compute to serve than Opus 5, and its pricing reflects that. Our tests show that at default settings it will cost 40% less than Opus 5 on typical workloads. items.body: AI news today, November 5, 2026: data centers lost the midterms, Google is fighting a school Search backlash, and OpenAI agreed to buy Pierre Computer. Here are the 10 top stories and 5 security stories, each with free, non-paywalled sources. Google is responding to political backlash after reports that it would disable Search for schools that reject its AI tools. The company said Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search are off by default, and schools can turn one or all of them back on. We first covered the policy in our November 4 briefing . Critics including Bernie Sanders, Zohran Mamdani and former FTC chair Lina Khan called the policy extortion and monopoly abuse. Google education vice president Chris Phillips told The New York Times that Search and AI are "deeply integrated." Google says AI Overviews will add guided-learning steps. Why it matters: Schools now face a package deal: accept classroom AI or lose the search tool students and teachers already use. Voters rejected data center expansion across the country. In 45 local ballot measures, 33 will restrict development, according to Redbud Consulting data cited by The Verge. NBC's Election Day poll found 76% of voters opposed data centers in their communities. We first covered the backlash in our October 24 briefing . Texas elected Gina Hinojosa, who backs a statewide moratorium. Michigan elected Abdul El-Sayed, who wants a pause on new projects. Ohio returned Sherrod Brown, who attacked his opponent over data centers. Some pro-development candidates still won, including Florida Governor-elect Byron Donalds. Wells, Maine, backed a 180-day moratorium on large data centers. Why it matters: AI's power bottleneck is becoming a political bottleneck, and developers now face local votes before they face grid queues. OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, the startup behind Code Storage and the open-source Trees, Diffs and Highlights libraries. Trees and Diffs already power file browsing and change review in the Codex app. Code Storage lets apps store code and track its history with Git. Financial terms were not disclosed. OpenAI plans to fold Code Storage into Codex after closing and keep Pierre's open-source projects open. Existing Code Storage customers can keep using the service during the transition. items.body: .NET 8 and .NET 9 will reach end of support on November 10, 2026 . After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide servicing updates, security fixes, or technical support for these versions. We recommend upgrading to .NET 10 , which is an LTS release supported through November 2028. By upgrading, you will continue receiving security updates and servicing fixes to keep your applications protected. .NET 8 is a Long Term Support (LTS) release, supported for 36 months from its initial release in November 2023. That support window closes on November 10, 2026 . .NET 9 is a Standard Term Support (STS) release. As we announced , STS releases now get 24 months of support instead of 18. That puts .NET 9 end of support on the same day: November 10, 2026 . November 10th is a Patch Tuesday release day. .NET 8 and .NET 9 may each receive one final update on that day if there is a known critical issue. Starting with a future servicing update for Visual Studio 2022, the .NET 8 and .NET 9 components will be marked as out of support. Existing installations won’t be affected. You will need to retarget to .NET 10 (or later) to stay supported. You can use the “remove out of support components” option in Visual Studio to clean up .NET 8 and .NET 9 from existing installations. You can upgrade your app to .NET 10 by changing the value of the TargetFramework property in your project file to net10.0 . You will also need to update your development and hosting environments. This process is covered in more detail in Upgrade to a new .NET version . <PropertyGroup> <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework> </PropertyGroup> Using .NET 8 or .NET 9 apps If you’re using a .NET 8 or .NET 9 app, we recommend reaching out to the software developer or vendor who produced it to ask for an updated version that uses .NET 10 is available. .NET 8 and .NET 9 will both reach end of support on November 10, 2026. items.body: Search the site Donate Close Search How would you best describe that thing you're looking for? EU governments have agreed on their position on the Digital Omnibus, retaining changes that threaten fundamental rights to privacy and data protection. With negotiations moving to the European Parliament, MEPs must reject the proposed weakening of GDPR safeguards for AI and pseudonymised data, protect individual rights, and defend ePrivacy against new tracking exemptions. Genuine simplification should make our rights easier to exercise and enforce, not give companies more freedom to exploit our data. When the European Commission presented its Digital Omnibus in November 2025, it promised to simplify Europe’s digital rules without weakening fundamental rights. Yet, as EDRi and others warned at the time , a majority of its proposals, particularly those regarding General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and ePrivacy, went far beyond reducing administrative burdens. They are part and parcel of a broad deregulatory wave that is devouring most of our rights and safeguards in the name of empty promises of competitiveness and sovereignty. On 21 October 2026, EU governments agreed on their negotiating position , which has timidly corrected some of the Commission’s most questionable choices, but has mainly endorsed changes that could make exploiting personal data easier while making abuses even harder to challenge. The result is a deal that weakens important safeguards and makes redress harder. There is also little evidence that weakening these protections will improve Europe’s competitiveness. Some changes may instead reinforce the advantages of Big Tech companies that already control and abuse enormous volumes of information about us and the people around us. We have put together a comprehensive, multi-column table comparing the existing legislation, the European Commission’s proposed changes, and what the Council has actually agreed to, topping it up all with EDRi’s position on both proposals. The Council retained a dedicated provision, Article 88bis (Article 88c in the Commission’s proposal), explicitly recognising the possibility of relying on the GDPR’s ‘legitimate interest’ legal basis to use personal data when developing or operating AI systems. Under the GDPR, companies can already use this legal basis in certain circumstances, provided they demonstrate a legitimate interest, prove that processing is necessary, and establish that people’s rights do not override that interest. items.body: The European Commission aims to foster an environment where online platforms thrive, treat users fairly and take action to limit the spread of illegal content. Online platforms are strong drivers of innovation and play an important role in Europe's digital society and economy. They cover a wide range of activities including online marketplaces, social media, creative content outlets, app stores, price comparison websites, platforms for the collaborative economy as well as search engines. They increase consumer choice, improve efficiency and competitiveness of industry and can enhance civil participation in society. Online platforms share key characteristics, such as the use of information and communication technologies to facilitate interactions between users, collection and use of data about such interactions, and network effects. These network effects make the use of the platforms with most users most valuable to other users. Today, 1 million EU businesses are already selling goods and services via online platforms, and more than 50% of small and medium enterprises selling through online marketplaces sell cross-border. The European Commission's approach to online platforms focuses on fostering a trusting, lawful and innovation-driven environment in the EU. To this end, the Commission identified key areas of interest in its Communication on Online Platforms . The guiding policy principles are: The Digital Services Act (DSA) entered into application in February 2024. Together with a Digital Markets Act (DMA) , the DSA will create a safer and more open digital space for all users and ensure a level playing field for businesses. The regulation on online platform-to-business relationships puts in place a harmonised framework for minimum transparency and redress rights. It protects companies that depend on online platforms for reaching consumers, while safeguarding the innovation potential of platforms. In November 2025, to simplify digital rules, the Commission proposed to repeal of the P2B Regulation. Both the Digital Services Act (DSA) and the Digital Markets Act (DMA) have introduced more effective and far-reaching rules to ensure a safe, predictable and trusted online environment, as well as contestable and fair digital markets. The Commission issued a Recommendation on measures to effectively tackle illegal content online in March 2018. This builds on the Communication on tackling illegal content online of September 2017, translating political commitment into (non-binding) legal form.
